accent: Retained 6.4.71 augment supplies high a. TS rite formula and the Mādhyandina text mark independent initial high in this predicate.
Received high belongs to ma; TS and Śākala reproduce the high-plus-follower pattern. No transfer of an ā-upasarga accent is needed.
Śākala places pitch of the adjacent accusative on final a; attached finite syllable with svarita is distinct from an independently accented kṛta.
Taittirīya preserves the accusative high and its following svarita despite the different velar nasal display.
The fragment containing the preverb retains its own high while the verbal carrier in the direct pada is unaccented. The reading retains separate orthoepic identities.
syntax: Śākala yadi conditional assigns an afflicted person to āmayati; the herbs supply the 2pl of the remedy predicate.
TS Sāyaṇa takes what afflicts like disease as the object removed by the herbs' 2pl.
The bare request supplies imam as affected person, agadam as predicative outcome and me as beneficiary.
RV annotators and Sāyaṇa admit the finite affliction predicate inside the subordinate clause.
The Śukla commentaries allow āmayāvini nare as the host of disease. Mahīdhara's śatṛ designation permits the morphologically identical locative analysis.
Ritual workers are the third-plural subject of akran in Śatapatha Sāyaṇa's gloss; karman is what they performed.
Bhaṭṭabhāskara preserves the heard plural with a dyad and an interpretive person shift tied to the ensuing preṭa instruction. This leaves the actual received P3pl unchanged.
Eṣā and uktā identify the nominative singular expiation.
Imāḥ and the request śṛṇuta identify the accusative plural expiations.
A lexical inflectional analogy at the two Vedic predicate NOMpl addresses keeps their stha agreement, separate from the Classical command's object ACCpl.
contact: The Śākala outcome keeps the padānta anusvāra after 8.3.23. It belongs to the accusative noun.
Taittirīya gives the velar outcome in the transmitted rendering under the optional padānta parasavarṇa route of 8.4.58–59.
At word-final t, jaś supplies d under 8.2.39 before the vowel. The long ā is already on the lexical affliction stem.
observations: Mahīdhara expressly reads laṭ with śap elision; Uvaṭa and Sāyaṇa preserve its directive paraphrase.
The comparative print treats kṛtha as a back-formed root present and supports priority of the transmitted tha reading.
Independent bare P2pl kṛta is attested in the make-well request of both recensions and matches Macdonell's root-aorist imperative example.
Nyāsa's explanation selects cli and the presence of the aorist inventory without sic's functions. Its kṛ example gives the jhi and final-cluster analysis.
The exact akran stanza is located in TS 1.8.3, VSM 3.47 and ŚBM 2.5.2.29; the second half has sudānavaḥ versus sacābhuvaḥ.
Bhaṭṭabhāskara explicitly names the chli-luk rule and a dual intended participant count/person shift. ŚB Sāyaṇa instead gives an actual third-person finite gloss.
The root list has am roge in curādi with its numbering disagreement. Kaumudī separately derives the homographic movement-root causative.
Mahīdhara's śatṛ statement and Uvaṭa's locative gloss ground an additional locative reading beside the received Śākala finite analysis.
Two descriptions explicitly license a small group of short-i nominatives in īs on the pattern of derivative ī.
TS Sāyaṇa explains the sam-qualified herbs through fitness to do their work, while the exact pada separates sam from the nominal stem.
The paired cases and their agreement give a second classical meaning and one identical surface with different case.
Brahmamuni states jas→śas for the adjacent RV oṣadhīḥ. The Taittirīya opening uses the ordinary oṣadhayaḥ.
decisions: Separate the indicative root-present shape with aspirated tha and the active root-aorist request with dental ta. Directive translation does not alter the received ending.
The selected aorist removes chli before sic under 2.4.80. The middle-ending ta/thās exception under 2.4.79 has no jurisdiction at these P positions.
Use selected chandas augment absence for the two requests and actual augmented aṅga at akran. These are different typed augment records.
Keep P3pl on the named mantra and preserve Bhaṭṭabhāskara's relational analysis as a separate scope of speaker and participants.
Select am roge curādi lexical ṇic and its non-mit history. The independently licensed homographic bhvādi causative remains separately addressed.
Make a distinct weak locative śatṛ key on the named Śukla analysis while retaining the finite P3sg case elsewhere.
Use a case-conditioned derivative-ī-type readout on only the two exact NOMpl slots. The Pāṇinian precedence question remains Open.
The śas-owned short-i expiation ACCpl and the Vedic NOMpl both give īs on separate case histories; preserve both senses and scopes.
Treat the oṣadhīḥ jas→śas as its own positive commentary control and keep its transfer to the two remedy words Open.
